articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Centers
articles.text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] has just started! Not off to a good start? Don't worry, I am here to help you! You have four trades, so let's use them wisely. This may be the help you need to bounce back! Here's a quick review of my center picks from Round 1. Jonas Valanciunas was a slam dunk as he marked his return to the EuroLeague with 26.4 fantasy points and a gain of 0.4 credits. Kevarrius Hayes was also a clever pick as he went for 13.2 fantasy points and gained 0.2 credits, while Allan Dokossi was nearly as good with 12 fantasy points and a gain of 0.1 credits. Moses Wright hurt a lot of us with just 9 fantasy points, which caused him to lose 0.3 credits and I was too high on Austin Wiley, who ran into foul trouble, scored just 4.4 fantasy points and lost 0.3 credits. My advice is not limited to big men. Go see my [guard] and [forward] recommendations. Here is who I like at center in Round 2: ### Mathias Lessort, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (15.0 credits) It is a very simple decision to make: if you have the credits, you should go for [Mathias Lessort]. First, he is a T2 player, so if Vezen... if your captain doesn't play well, then you have a great choice with a very high floor. Lessort was at his very best in Round 1 with 15 points, 9 rebounds, 3 blocks and 9 fouls drawn against Paris. Who will stop him from now on? ### Dan Oturu, Hapoel Tel Aviv (14.9 credits) [Dan Oturu] had an outstanding first quarter against Bayern with 9 points and 8 rebounds. He looked on his way to be MVP of the Round, but slowed down and Hapoel didn't win. He finished that game with huge numbers: 20 points on 10-of-11 two-point shooting, 12 rebounds and 2 blocks for a PIR of 32. Oturu is Coach Itoudis's number one choice at center. He should be on your team. ### Olek Balcerowski, FC Barcelona (8.3 credits) If you need a cheaper option, then you can go for [Olek Balcerowski], who had a couple of really good performances last week. He opened the EuroLeague season with a bang: 10 points and 4 rebounds for a PIR of 14 against Efes. Balcerowski did even better in the Spanish League with 21 points and 6 rebounds for a PIR of 30. Josh Nebo is out, so it's Balcerowski's time in fantasy. ### Johannes Voigtmann, FC Bayern Munich (7.9 credits) Yes, Bayern plays against Fenerbahce, but it comes off a big win against Hapoel on [Johannes Voigtmann]'s go-ahead three-pointer. He made the most of his 19 minutes on the floor with 10 points, 5 rebounds and 3 assists for a PIR of 17, while making few mistakes. Voigtmann has a lot of talent and experience, and comes off a game-winning shot. At his price, he is a good option. ### Kevarrius Hayes, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (7.5 credits) Last week, we talked about Partizan centers and how they would split minutes. Well, with Joffrey Lauvergne sidelined, [Kevarrius Hayes] and Tonye Jekiri are seeing more playing time and making the most of it. Hayes started in Round 1, finishing the game against Milan with 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting and 3 rebounds for a PIR of 12. Definitely not bad for 7.5 credits, right?

articles.text: The 2026-27 EuroLeague is underway and so is the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. I know, Round 1 left some disappointments but now, you have four trades to improve your team. Even better, I are here to help you with some fantasy tips. MY picks at forward were disappointing for me too. Though I did well to recommend Eleftherios Mantzoukas of Panathinaikos, that's where the success ended. Mantzoukas scored 13.2 fantasy points and gained 0.3 credits. Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot (5 fantasy points, lost 0.4 credits), Joel Parra (0 fantasy points, lost 0.3 credits) and Jordan Nwora (8 fantasy points, lost 0.2 credits) all hurt their owners and the only reasons that Stefan Joksimovic (-1 fantasy points) didn’t lose credits is because he started at the minimum price. Yikes! I am determined to do better in all my picks this time. My recommendations at [guard] and [center] are already live and here are five forwards for the future for all budgets. ### Dario Saric, Anadolu Efes Istanbul (14.9 credits) That is the way you come back to the EuroLeague, with a huge game and leaving no doubt about your ability. [Dario Saric] had a strong Round 1 game against Barca with 17 points on 8-of-9 free throw shooting, 5 rebounds and 7 fouls drawn for a PIR of 26. He was also great in his team's Turkish League opener with 16 points and a PIR of 25. Real is up next, so expect him to keep leading Efes. ### Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas (11.6 credits) Frankie Sachs always talks about sensational sophomores in the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge podcast. [Azuolas Tubelis] had an outstanding first season and is determined to do even better now. He proved it in Round 1 against Zvezda with 10 points, 12 rebounds, 4 assists and a PIR of 23. At just 11.6 credits, Tubelis is a great opportunity for all fantasy managers out there. ### Tadas Sedekerskis, Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (10.5 credits) After an injury-plagued year, [Tadas Sedekerskis] is back and seems to be in good shape, too. He showed that against Olympiacos with 15 points and a PIR of 14 in 20 minutes, and had similar numbers in the Spanish League, getting a PIR of 16 in just 16 minutes. Rebounds, effectiveness, steals and very few missed shot should make Sedekerskis a player to consider. ### Braxton Key, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul (8.6 credits) After a great SuperCup semifinal against Real, [Braxton Key] keeps pacing Fenerbahce in all official competition. He led Fenerbahce to a 78-68 come back over Virtus with 11 points, 10 rebounds and a PIR of 22. In his first-ever Turkish League game, Key kept rolling with 12 points and 5 assists for a PIR of 18. It is hard to find a better bargain in the forward market right now! ### Konstantinos Mitoglou, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (5.5 credits) First things first, Panathinaikos is a T2 team in Rounds 2 and 3, which makes its good options even better. [Konstantinos Mitoglou] stepped on court for over 18 minutes to get 11 points, 6 rebounds and a couple of steals for a PIR of 14. At just 5.5 credits, he is a must-have player if he keeps posting those numbers. Oh, and keep an eye on [Eleftherios Mantzoukas] at just 4.8 credits, too.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Guards
articles.text: Round 1 of the 2026-27 EuroLeague seasons is in the books and with it the first round of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge], too. Now we are heading into the first double-round week of the season. It is time to check the schedule, look for Turn 2 players who will deliver in Round 2, and reload your rosters before the next deadline, on Tuesday at 18:00 CET. My Round 1 picks were pretty good and three of them gained 0.2 credits! They were, TJ Shorts, who scored 22 fantasy points, Nigel Williams-Goss with 15.4 points and young Mario Saint-Supery with 11 fantasy points. Meanwhile Sylvain Francisco had 19.8 fantasy points and went up 0.1 credits. Alas, Matteo Spagnolo accounted for 7 fantasy points and his price remained the same. Here are five guards who deserve serious consideration for Round 2. I have made my picks at [forward] and [center], too. ### Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.9 credits) I said we would focus on T2 players, which means there will be a lot of Panathinaikos players in all fantasy articles this week. Panathinaikos is the heavy favorite to win both games at Telekom Center Athens. [Sylvain Francisco] signed for ASVEL early in the off-season and ended up playing for Panathinaikos. It should be a special game for him, so keep an eye on him. ### Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (14.5 credits) This is almost a no-brainer. [Carlik Jones] was the Round 1 MVP and even though Partizan plays twice on the road this week, it faces fast-paced teams in Paris and Bayern. He should keep leading Partizan the way he did in Round 1, making Jones a must for all fantasy teams. If you got him in Round 1, don't sell him. If you missed him, he is still affordable, so go for it. ### Scottie Wilbekin, Besiktas Istanbul (7.7 credits) In recent years, [Scottie Wilbekin] may not have been the best fantasy player, but at 7.7 credits, it is hard to ignore a player of his caliber. He had a solid Round 1 game against Valencia, getting a PIR of 13, and goes against Maccabi in Round 2. Wilbekin remains Maccabi's all-time top scorer in the EuroLeague with 1,801 points. Talent and motivation always go well together! ### Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne (5.3 credits) This is a surprise that few saw coming. [Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada] took over in Round 1, leading ASVEL to an 84-74 home win over Maccabi with 14 points, 5 assists and a PIR of 17 as a starter, playing over 21 minutes. An isolated good game? Think again. Fodzo Dada also played almost 21 minutes in French League action, too. All aboard the Fodzo Dada train! ### Dovydas Giedraitis, Zalgiris Kaunas (4.3 credits) Owned by just 1.3% of fantasy managers at the moment, [Dovydas Giedraitis] is a very cheap option that should allow you to afford other players. [Nigel Williams-Goss] is sidelined for Zalgiris, which opens the door for Giedraitis, who started and played 20 minutes in the Lithuanian League on Sunday. Giedraitis is a cheap get for all fantasy managers.

articles.text: As I always did, I’m just going to ignore some of the obvious expensive options like Sasa Vezenkov, Jonas Valanciunas, Sylvain Francisco, Mike James, etc. Round 2 has a particularity, cause only 4 teams will have their matchup in Turn 2, so that means we have to think about players to captain in those 4 teams, to be able to have a decent captain in both turns. I always like to include those players who are not that obvious or if they are, at least in the moment I recommend them is one of the best moments of the season, based on matchup streak, current shape, etc. I also tend to not repeat the ones I recommended last round, so take all this into account. 🧠GUARDS Chris Jones (12.6 cr): On the roster analysis for Zvezda I already talked about him possibly nearing his prime on this Zvezda, and I was not far from the truth. He has started the season in a really great way, showing leadership as playmaker, but also confience on the scoring side. He might not be the one with the biggest usage, but I think that will increase gradually. Theo Maledon (10 cr): We predicted Theo being one of the players taking a step forward with Pedro Martínez and that’s what we’ve seen until now. He did an amazing preseason, now he has started the season in an unbeatable way, being the best player in both games played so far (EL & ACB). Devon Hall (8.5 cr): We’ve already seen the usage coach Poetta will give him, so that added to his capacity to contribute from every aspect of the game, makes him a great option. He might not be the best scorer, but I think he’s a pretty safe player, as he probably won’t get a -5 FPTS game. Maodo Lo (7.1 cr): After finding out the 2-weeks injury of Nigel Williams-Goss, the first direct replacement that comes to my mind is Maodo Lo, who should be the one to get his minutes. He might not be on his best career moment, but he has the quality and talent to put up a really great performance as playmaker. Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada (5.3 cr): He seemed to have a really quick adaptation to top-level basketball and a pretty decent usage to be that young, so it looks like a great option on that price. He’ll play in Turn 2, so that makes it even better as a Round 2 choice, even though teammates like Patty Mills could be the musts. 🎯FORWARDS Kameron Taylor (12.6 cr): His last season was really good, but he started this one even better, so I think on a team where he might be one of the scoring references during all the season and with his rebounding capacity, the ceiling is really far from where he’s right now. Alec Peters (12 cr): While Garrison Mathews remains sidelined, he might be one of the best Forwards available in Fantasy terms. His playing time is already pretty high (30 mins) and will keep being like this as long as Mathews is injured. He just need to contribute a little bit more in rebounding and defensively to become the ultimate choice. Kessler Edwards (10 cr): He’s a really complete PF that already got a massive performance on this season Italian Supercup vs Milano (25 EFF). He can get +10 FPTS without even scoring, so imagine the potential if he gets a great game in terms of scoring, on a game that will be easier for him than Fener. Dinos Mitoglou (5.9 cr): He started the season in a really great shape, with the confidence he was missing last season, so being that cheap and while NHD keeps sidelined, he could have really great performances as he’s good on rebounding, but also on mid-range and 3pt shooting. 🗼CENTERS Mathias Lessort (15 cr): He’s an obvious choice, but especially this round against ASVEL and being probably the best captain option for Round 2, Turn 2. He seems to be again nearing his prime and that means the ceiling of this guy is still really far from 15 credits, so it might be time to select him. O. Balcerowski (8.3 cr) : As Nebo keeps sidelined, he’s performing on surprising numbers in both EuroLeague & ACB first games, so he might be one of the best mid-price centers right now. Great rebounding capacity and accompanied by pretty good playmakers in terms of creating spaces for him to end up alone under the basket. Jasiel Rivero (7.5 cr): Two great rounds ahead for Valencia facing 2 of the “weakest” teams on paper and especially Baskonia being a really bad frontcourt defender. That makes Jasiel a really good option to consider in cheap options, as he could be in advantage under the basket quite a lot of times. Thanks for reading EuroBallin' Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

articles.text: Opening night of the 2026-27 EuroLeague season is in the books and Thursday's slate of games already delivered its share of heroes and heartbreak – especially for [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers. Whether you're basking in the glow of a breakout performance from a value pick or nursing the wounds of a big-money bust who no-showed, every fantasy manager has a story to tell after night one. Let's break down which players padded your scoreline and which ones left you searching for the bench button. Here are Thursday’s fantasy winners and losers: ### Fantasy winners #### [Tyler Dorsey, Olympiacos Piraeus] Last season, Dorsey scored at least 20 points in his first two games. He started strong again this season with 25 points on excellent shooting to finish with 31.9 fantasy points. Though Dorsey is not a cheap player, coming in at 12.6 credits, he provided plenty of value to the 3.5% of owners who signed him for Round 1. #### [Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne] Still a teenager, Fodzo Dada posted a manly performance for ASVEL at home with 14 points and 5 assists for 18.7 fantasy points, which cost a mere 4.8 credits! I recommended him on the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast], but what can I do that only 1.1% of owners took my advice? I am pretty sure that number will rise this week, but you will be buying him at a higher price. #### [Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas] While all the attention was on his frontcourt mate [Jonas Valanciunas], Tubelis was almost as productive, but at a significant discount. The Zalgiris power forward posted 10 points and a career-high 12 rebounds, recording his second EuroLeague double-double, while totaling 25.3 fantasy points. That’s quite a haul for his 11.1-credit price tag. Tubelis was owned by 6.5% of fantasy owners, and those managers were winners on Thursday, too. ### Fantasy losers #### [Johnathan Motley, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade] Center is not always an easy fantasy position. And if you were among the 2.5% of fantasy owners who had Motley in your lineup, it became a nightmare position for you on Thursday. One in 40 fantasy teams spent 11.0 credits on a center who recorded minus-13 fantasy points. Ouch! Even though in almost all cases Motley will wind up on the fantasy bench (every owner who has a pulse and a phone will bench him on Friday), which will mitigate the damage, this performance will also result in lost credits. Ouch again! #### [Nikola Milutinov, Olympiacos Piraeus] I don’t know why, but 2.6% of fantasy owners had Milutinov this week despite the injury concerns. In the end, he played 9 minutes off the bench and scored 3.3 fantasy points. His owners paid 15.3 credits for that. Milutinov was the sixth-highest priced player in the game and will be among the lowest-scoring fantasy players in Round 1. From a credit standpoint, it would have been better for his owners had Milutinov not played at all. #### [Joel Parra, FC Barcelona] This one hurt a lot of fantasy players because Parra is the second-most-owned player in Round 1 at a whopping 30.9%! Parra started and played nearly 27 minutes, which is great for a player who cost 7.0 credits. However, on Thursday he shot poorly, missing 8 of the 10 shots he took. That left him with a fantasy score of 0. Well, at least his owners have plenty of company.

With Kendrick Nunn sidelined by injury, Sylvain Francisco is primed to step up and direct the Greek side’s backcourt rotation. Factoring in the high-tempo matchup against Paris and his expanded role, Francisco projects to log around 30 minutes on court, giving him clear upside to comfortably surpass the 20 fantasy point threshold in Round 1. Carlik Jones – Partizan – 13.6 credits Carlik Jones enters the new EuroLeague season as the clear focal point of Partizan’s attack, expected to handle the bulk of primary creation responsibilities. Partizan enjoys a very manageable schedule over the opening three rounds, giving them a solid runway to build early momentum. However, their overall offensive efficiency will heavily rely on Jones producing at an elite, high-usage level. Opening Round 1 at home against Milano, expect Jones to be fully motivated to put on a dominant show in front of the Belgrade crowd, making him a prime fantasy pick. Shorts , DeJulius should be able to leverage his size advantage to consistently force mismatches, collapse defenses, and generate quality scoring looks. Given his role as a creator, if he manages to post a PIR around 15, he will firmly solidify himself as a high-value budget option for Round 1. articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Difficulty Rating from Round 1 to Round 6
articles.text: Preparations for the new season are in full swing, and Basketball Sphere is set to deliver the most comprehensive EuroLeague Fantasy coverage throughout the entire 2026/27 campaign. Our goal is to provide you with all the data and insights needed to build a championship-caliber team and make smart decisions round after round. Alongside our team-by-team breakdowns, each day will bring a new dedicated topic to keep you ahead of the competition. We will systematically cover every critical angle for your draft and weekly lineups. Through these deep dives, you will gain key insights into coaching tactics and rotation roles – the crucial factors that drive Fantasy output. One of the key factors in building a successful Fantasy team is analyzing the schedule. That is why, throughout the season, Basketball Sphere will feature Difficulty Rating tables showing the difficulty of every EuroLeague team’s schedule over the upcoming rounds. The first unlimited transfers will be available after Round 6, the second after Round 13, the third after Round 18, the fourth after Round 23, the fifth after Round 28, and the sixth after Round 34. In this article, we have prepared the schedule difficulty for the opening six rounds, up to the first set of unlimited transfers, and this will be our practice throughout the entire season. EuroLeague Fantasy Basketball Sphere Competiton: JOIN the Challenge and Win Prizes Green indicates favorable matchups against somewhat easier opponents or games that are expected to produce a high number of points. Red indicates a tough opponent who should be avoided at that particular moment, while gray represents a matchup of medium difficulty. If a team has several green squares in a row, it means they have a run of particularly favorable matchups. The same applies to red squares, only in the opposite direction. Favorable schedule Analyzing the schedule difficulty over the opening six rounds of the EuroLeague Fantasy season reveals several key targets for fantasy managers. Panathinaikos stands out as the premier team to target, boasting a remarkably favorable schedule, particularly across the first three rounds. Targeting their core contributors early provides a strong foundation for high early-round output. Beyond Greens, managers should look toward Milano , Valencia , and Partizan . Players from these rosters present excellent utility and strong point-scoring potential over the opening stretch. Meanwhile, Virtus requires a more patient strategy. Their schedule turns extremely favorable from Rounds 4 to 6, turning their key rotation players into prime hidden gems and top differential targets once the initial rounds conclude. Tracking these schedule shifts will give managers a distinct competitive edge. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Will Have Smaller Roles Compared to Their Previous Teams Unfavorable schedule Analyzing unfavorable early schedules reveals that Anadolu Efes immediately stands out with a very difficult initial run. Their sole favorable matchup arrives in Round 5 against Bayern , making their assets primary fade options for fantasy managers. Bayern and Virtus also face tough opening slates. However, Virtus’ brutal schedule across the first three rounds could actually work to fantasy managers’ advantage. As challenging matchups lower their players’ output, price drops should follow. Consequently, key Virtus rotation options could turn into highly affordable, high-upside targets from Rounds 4 to 6. Capitalizing on these initial price dips allows managers to secure valuable differential assets right as their schedule turns dramatically positive. articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips Round 1
articles.text: As I always did, I’m just going to ignore some of the obvious expensive options like Sasa Vezenkov, Jonas Valanciunas, Sylvain Francisco, Mike James, etc. I always like to include those players who are not that obvious or if they are, at least in the moment I recommend them is one of the best moments of the season, based on matchup streak, current shape, etc. 🧠GUARDS TJ Shorts (14.9 cr): He’s a expensive, yet obvious choice in guard position, I know. However, I include him just because I think he’s the best guard option on the game this season, as he managed to land on a team where can be the real TJ we’ve seen in Paris or Bonn. A player that has a main role, the ball is on his hands most of the time, so he can decide what to do on almost each offensive play. Points and assists will never be lacking from him, so I think he’s also a safe bet, as he’ll be quite consistent. Carlik Jones (13.6 cr): Similar reasons to the ones I mentioned for TJ. He’ll have a mian role on a team where he’s the clear leader in terms of playmaking and scoring. He has a good relationship with the fans and coach Peñarroya, so he’ll be high on confidence and will be used a lot in EuroLeague, so perfect mix. Vasilije Micic (12 cr): His preseason has been quite brutal, averaging 21 PIR in 4 games played. That makes me think he could be again on full confidence and we could see the MVP version of Micic on a team that has a long guard rotation, but needs a player like him to work really well. I know it’s a risk cause last season he was terrible, but I can see another face on Vasilije this season. Trent Forrest (10.6 cr): One of the most complete players, with a crazy ability to take profit from each and every minute he’s on the court. In terms of FPTS/min he’s one of the best choices, so knowing that Saras loves players like him, he could have a really outstanding season in terms of efficiency. The only risk is the scoring side, cause there are games where he just focus on the playmaking area and takes few shots. Iffe Lundberg (8.3 cr): A really complete combo guard who can contribute from every aspect of the game, so that makes him a great choice. He’ll have a big usage with Kattash, but don’t expect massive performances from him, as he’s strength is his consistency on good performances, but most of them around 10-20 FPTS. He will play in Turn 2 of Round 2, so he’s a great pick thinking for both rounds at the same time. Matteo Spagnolo (6.4 cr): Amazing preseason being one of the leaders of this short Baskonia roster and having the trust of coach Galbiati on him. He’s a full package player, as he’s really good rebounding and assisting, but sometimes also on the scoring side, which makes him a great steal on low-priced players. I could also add some interesting names like Mario Saint-Supéry (4.7) , Andrés Feliz (6.2) , Leandro Bolmaro (8.7), Tremont Waters (9.9), Matthew Strazel (10.3) or Horton-Tucker (12.7). 🎯FORWARDS Jordan Nwora (13 cr): Might be on his best moment since landing in Europe, as he’s confidence and efficiency on the scoring side is mindblowing, averaging 17.8 pts in 5 games. He also has a really great capacity to rebound, so that makes him a really good choice for a high-usage player that in my opinion is really underpriced right now. Nikola Mirotic (11.6 cr): One of the most notable players in Europe this last decade and one of the most Fantasy-friendly players ever, as he drawns a massive amount of fouls by game, he has an outstanding rebounding capacity and on the scoring side no doubt that he’s one of the best PF on the league. I think 11.6 is not his real price and his ceiling is way higher, even more on a roster like the Valencia one. Bonzie Colson (11.3 cr): His preseason has been excellent, showing that he’s the main SF on rotation and that he’s on a really great moment on his career in terms of scoring, but also on the rebounding side. He averaged 14.8 PIR in 5 games grabbing 4.2 reb and scoring 15.2 ppg, which are really correct numbers. Eugene Omoruyi (10.5 cr): Even though his preseason has not been the best in the end, he started in a really great way, showing that he’ll be the main PF for coach Alimpijevic, especially in EuroLeague. Last season he showed his efficiency on court with Baskonia and this season in Besiktas he’ll have a similar role, so this is my risky bid for the start of the season. Braxton Key (8 cr): What a SuperCup for him and preseason overall too, showing one of the most complete versions of himself. He comes after a massive end of season with Valencia leading that playoff serie against Pao and now he faces a new season on a team where the rotation is bigger, but he might take a main role and be really efficient. Joel Parra (7 cr): Now we’re in front of the best Forward option right now. A player that last season already showed his quality, but he started this season unbelievably well. His confidence to take the important shots, no regrets on 3pt shooting, the energy on defense and offensive rebounding, the ability to take the ball out and bring some assists, etc. Everything is looking well on him this start of the season. I would add Azuolas Tubelis (11.1) , Kessler Edwards (10), Miles Norris (8.9) , Lamar Stevens (8), Tyson Ward (7.5) & Dinos Mitoglou (5.5). 🗼CENTERS Moses Wright (14 cr): The must on this center position, as he has been the best player during this preseason, he comes after a massive breakout season in Zalgiris and in my opinion, he’s the most dominant center in Europe right now. He will be used a lot as he’s the main center and has really great playmakers to feed even more his scoring quality under the basket. Donta Hall (10.9 cr): Even if Milutinov is ready to play on this opening round of the season, Hall is on a level right now that’s pretty crazy. He does not need to play a lot, to get massive efficiency performances like the ones he did on this preseason averaging 18.2 PIR per game. So if Milu is out, he’s a must, if Milu can play, he remains a great option on this price range. Bruno Fernando (10.3 cr): Finally having the main role he wanted in Europe, accompanied by 2 of the best playmakers in the league, makes him one of the best options. He’s a really powerful center with a great rebounding capacity and improving day by day his scoring efficiency on the paint. He will have a high-usage with Laso, so I think you should all consider him for your teams. Nikola Tanaskovic (7.8 cr): A big sleeper in my opinion, as he comes after a really great season in EuroCup with Buducnost and as we saw in this preseason, he will have the trust of coach Peñarroya. He’s a player that really takes advantage from each and every minute that he’s on the court, so on that price, he could deliver really great performances. Thanks for reading EuroBallin' Substack! • Ο Νίκολα Μιλουτίνοφ τέθηκε εκτός δράσης για τη «διαβολοβδομάδα» λόγω ενοχλήσεων στο ισχίο, αυξάνοντας τον χρόνο των Χολ και Ντάνστον στον Ολυμπιακό.
• Εξαιρετικά αμφίβολη παραμένει η συμμετοχή του Χουάντσο Ερνανγκόμεθ στον Παναθηναϊκό, καθιστώντας τον Ντίνο Μήτογλου περιζήτητη budget επιλογή στα φόργουορντ.
• Σημαντικές απουσίες αντιμετωπίζει η Παρτίζαν (Γουίλις, Λοβέρν, Μαρίνκοβιτς), οδηγώντας στην προσθήκη του Μπάντζα Σι και σε αυξημένες ευθύνες για τους Στίβενς και Χέις.
• Ο τραυματισμός του Νάιτζελ Ουίλιαμς-Γκος ανοίγει χώρο στην περιφέρεια της Ζάλγκιρις για τους Μάοντο Λο και Ντοβίντας Γκιεντράιτις.
• Οι απουσίες των Νέμπο και Μακουντού στη γραμμή ψηλών της Μπαρτσελόνα ενισχύουν τη fantasy αξία των Μπαλτσερόφσκι και Ενκαμχουά.
• Ο Σάσα Βεζένκοφ και ο Ματίας Λεσόρ ξεχωρίζουν ως οι κορυφαίες επιλογές αρχηγού για το 1ο και 2ο Turn αντίστοιχα.
• Σταθερές και δημοφιλείς επιλογές στα γκαρντ για τη 2η αγωνιστική παραμένουν οι Τι Τζέι Σορτς, Σιλβέν Φρανσίσκο και Κάρλικ Τζόουνς.
